result.target_topic: Q4 2024 Net Interest Income Performance and Drivers
result.target_summary: Citi's Q4 2024 net interest income was $13.7 billion (reported) or $13.8 billion (TEB), a decrease of $0.1 billion from the prior year, primarily driven by higher funding costs in Markets Fixed Income trading inventory, partially offset by non-Markets growth. The non-Markets increase was due to card loan growth in USPB and higher yields on reinvested securities, offset by investment securities losses from portfolio repositioning.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net interest income and yield performance in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income decreased by $871 million to $56.1 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, with net interest yield on a fully taxable-equivalent basis dropping 13 basis points to 1.95 percent. These declines were primarily driven by higher deposit costs, which were partially offset by higher asset yields and increased net interest income from Global Markets activity.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and Bank of America both reported decreases in Net Interest Income for 2024. Citi's NII decreased by $0.1 billion, primarily driven by Markets funding costs, while BAC's NII decreased by $871 million, primarily driven by higher deposit costs. Both companies also noted that these declines were partially offset by positive factors, such as non-Markets growth for Citi and Global Markets activity for BAC.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net Interest Income Growth and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income for 2024 was $8.06 billion, representing a 27% increase from 2023, driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates, partially offset by a decrease in deposits with banks.
comparisons.comparison: While Citi reported a decrease in total Net Interest Income (NII), Goldman Sachs reported a 27% increase in NII for 2024 ($8.06 billion vs $6.35 billion in 2023). Both disclosures detail the drivers of these changes: Citi's decrease was driven by funding costs offset by non-Markets growth, whereas GS's increase was driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates (gs_2024_7_P054_S003).

sentences.text: Citi's net interest income in the fourth quarter of 2024 was $13.7 billion on a reported basis and $13.8 billion on a taxable equivalent basis, a decrease of $0.1 billion from the prior-year period, primarily driven by Markets (down approximately $0.1 billion), partially offset by non-Markets (up approximately $0.04 billion).

Net interest income in the consolidated statements of earnings was $8.06 billion for 2024, 27% higher than 2023, reflecting an increase in interest income, partially offset by an increase in interest expense.

The increase in interest income primarily related to trading assets and investments (each reflecting the impact of higher average balances and higher average interest rates), collateralized agreements and other interest-earning assets (each reflecting the impact of higher average interest rates), partially offset by a decrease in interest income related to deposits with banks (reflecting the impact of lower average balances).

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Net Interest Revenue Performance and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Wealth Management net interest revenues decreased 10% year-over-year to $7,313 million in 2024, primarily driven by lower average sweep deposits, partially offset by higher investment portfolio yields and lending growth.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley disclosed net interest income/revenue performance drivers in 2024. Citi's non-Markets NII increased due to card loan growth and higher yields on reinvested securities (c_2024_7_P490_S001). Similarly, MS's Wealth Management net interest revenues decreased but were partially offset by 'higher yields on our investment portfolio and lending growth' (ms_2024_7_P064_S001). Both highlight the impact of portfolio composition and yield changes in their non-trading or wealth segments.
